name: The Peace Center
unique: A downtown performing arts campus with a concert hall, a theater and an outdoor amphitheater, booking Broadway tours, symphony, jazz and big name concerts on the Reedy.
buzz: The hall sounds excellent and the outdoor shows are a summer ritual. Check the schedule before a weekend trip.

name: Lake Conestee Nature Park
unique: Four hundred acres of wetland, forest and river floodplain on the Reedy, with boardwalks, gravel trails and more than 200 recorded bird species inside the city.
buzz: Flat, shady and free, with herons and turtles at every bend. The boardwalk section is stroller friendly.

name: Artisphere
unique: A three day downtown arts festival with juried artists, live music, food from local kitchens and demonstrations on the street.
buzz: One of the better art fairs in the Southeast, and downtown is walkable. Go Friday evening for the crowd.

name: Mast General Store
unique: A mountain general store chain that still sells cast iron, boots, candy by the scoop and everything else, in a downtown Greenville building with creaky floors.
buzz: It is a shopping stop, not an adventure, but the candy counter and the old fashioned hardware are fun for twenty minutes.

name: Laurens County Courthouse
unique: An 1838 courthouse on a square with a Confederate monument and old storefronts, still in use and largely unchanged.
buzz: The square is a five minute walk and the building is handsome. Pair it with the county museum.

name: Laurens Historic District
unique: A grid of Victorian houses, churches and commercial buildings around the courthouse square, in a town that grew on cotton and the railroad.
buzz: Quiet and well kept, with a good diner on the square. The walk is short but the architecture is real.

name: Union Historic District
unique: A main street of Victorian storefronts, a 1913 courthouse and churches, with the textile mill history that built the town still visible at the edges.
buzz: The downtown is small and quiet, and the mill history is the story. Pair it with Rose Hill.

name: Newberry Historic District
unique: A wide main street of Victorian commercial buildings, a 19th century courthouse and the opera house, laid out around a square that still holds a farmers market.
buzz: The opera house anchors a genuinely handsome downtown. Walk it before a show.

name: McCormick Historic District
unique: A planned mill town laid out by the McCormick family, with a grid of brick commercial buildings, a hotel and the gold mining history that preceded it.
buzz: Small and quiet, with the sense of a town built all at once. The old hotel is the landmark.

name: Lake Russell Recreation Area
unique: A Corps lake on the Savannah River with wooded shorelines, a swimming beach, boat ramps and campgrounds, less developed than the big reservoirs.
buzz: Quiet and cheap, with good bass and crappie fishing. The beach is small but calm.

name: Kings Mountain National Military Park
unique: The battlefield where backcountry militia stopped a British column in 1780, with a loop trail, earthworks, monuments and a museum.
buzz: The trail is paved and the story is well told. It is one of the most important battlefields most people have never visited.

name: Gaffney Historic District
unique: A downtown of brick storefronts, a 1900s courthouse and a railroad depot, with the giant peach water tower visible from blocks away.
buzz: The peach is the photo and the downtown is a quick walk. Good stop off I-85.

name: Chesterfield County Courthouse
unique: A Victorian courthouse with a clock tower on a small town square, surrounded by old storefronts and oaks.
buzz: A quick architectural stop on the way to Cheraw. The square is quiet.

name: Cheraw Market Hall
unique: An 1838 market hall on the river town's main street, part of a historic district of antebellum houses and churches.
buzz: The building is the anchor of the Cheraw walk. Look for the old theater and the Dizzy Gillespie marker nearby.

name: Marlboro County Courthouse
unique: A Romanesque courthouse with a clock tower on a square of Victorian storefronts, in a town settled by Scottish immigrants.
buzz: The square is handsome and quiet. Pair it with the county museum and Lake Wallace.

name: Dillon County Courthouse
unique: A neoclassical courthouse with columns and a dome on the main street of a tobacco and railroad town.
buzz: A quick stop on the way to the speedway. The main street has the bones of a busier era.

name: Dillon Main Street
unique: A wide main street of early 20th century brick buildings, a theater and a railroad depot, with the tobacco warehouses that made the town at the edges.
buzz: It is quiet, with a few good lunch counters. The depot is the photo.

name: Florence Little Theatre
unique: One of the oldest continuously running community theaters in the state, in a converted church with a small stage and a loyal company.
buzz: The productions are ambitious for a volunteer company and the room is intimate. Check the season.

name: Timrod Park
unique: A shaded city park with a lake, a rose garden, a playground and a statue of the poet Henry Timrod, next to the Florence library.
buzz: A pleasant lunch spot with ducks and shade. Not a destination, but a good break.

name: Darlington Public Square
unique: A courthouse square with a Confederate monument, Victorian storefronts and the old jail, in the town that gave NASCAR its toughest track.
buzz: The square is a quiet walk and the racing history is everywhere. Pair it with the raceway museum.

name: Coker University
unique: A small liberal arts campus with brick buildings, a lake and the Kalmia Gardens ravine at its edge, founded by the Coker family.
buzz: The campus is pretty and the gardens next door are the real draw. Park and walk.

name: Lancaster Historic District
unique: A courthouse square with a 1828 courthouse, Victorian storefronts and churches, in the town that surrendered to Sherman and was spared.
buzz: The square is small and well kept. The story of the surrender is on the markers.

name: Bob Doster's Backstreet Gallery
unique: A metal sculptor's gallery and yard full of welded animals, suns and figures, where the artist works in back and sells from the front.
buzz: The yard sculptures are the fun part and the artist is often there to talk. A good browse.

name: Rock Hill Old Town
unique: A revived main street with a fountain, a theater, a brewery and a market, plus a textile mill history that built the town.
buzz: The old town is walkable and busy on weekends. The velodrome and the river park are minutes away.

name: Lake Wylie
unique: The South Carolina shore of a 13,000 acre lake on the Catawba, with public ramps, coves and a shoreline of docks and hardwood.
buzz: The lake is the local summer and the sunsets are the postcard. Watch for shallow water near the river channel.

name: Broad River Paddle
unique: A broad, wooded river with shoals and sandbars, flowing past Revolutionary War crossings and pine forest, with put ins at Chester and Fish Dam Ford.
buzz: The current is gentle and the shoals are easy. Check the gauge and bring water.

name: Aiken County Historical Museum
unique: A museum in Banksia, a 1930s winter colony mansion, with rooms on the Aiken Institute, the Savannah River Site and the horse culture that made the town.
buzz: The house is the exhibit and the local history is well told. Free or nearly so.

name: Edgefield Historic Square
unique: A square of antebellum and Victorian buildings, a 19th century courthouse and a monument to the ten governors the town claims, with pottery studios nearby.
buzz: The governors claim is on every sign and the square is a pleasant walk. Pair it with the pottery.

name: Camden Historic District
unique: A colonial and Revolutionary War town with a wide main street, antebellum houses and the oldest inland town in the state, plus a horse culture that still runs on the weekends.
buzz: The architecture and the Revolutionary War sites are the draw. The Carolina Cup in spring is the social event.

name: Goodale State Park
unique: A cypress swamp lake with a canoe trail through old growth trees, a picnic area and a fishing pier, ten minutes from Camden.
buzz: The cypress tunnel is the paddle and it is easy. Bring bug spray in summer.

name: Lexington County Museum
unique: A village of relocated historic buildings, including a log cabin, a school and a cotton gin, on the grounds of the old Lexington courthouse.
buzz: The cluster of buildings makes the county's rural past tangible. Check hours before driving over.

name: Saluda Shoals Park
unique: A 400 acre river park on the Saluda with trails, a splash pad, canoe access and a nature center, inside the Columbia metro.
buzz: The river trail and the splash pad are the summer draws. Parking is cheap and the park is big enough to spread out.

name: Manchester State Forest
unique: A working pine forest with horse trails, dirt roads and the Poinsett bombing range history, next to Poinsett State Park.
buzz: The trails are sandy and quiet, good for horses and mountain bikes. Some areas close for hunting, so check.

name: Hampton Historic District
unique: A small grid of Victorian houses, a courthouse and churches around a town square, in the county that calls itself the birthplace of the watermelon festival.
buzz: Quiet and photogenic, best during the festival. The courthouse is the anchor.

name: Ridgeland Historic District
unique: A railroad town grid with a depot, a courthouse and Gullah Geechee history, halfway between Savannah and Charleston.
buzz: The depot and the old commercial block are the photo stops. Good break on the coastal drive.

name: Sgt. Jasper Park
unique: A riverfront park on the Savannah with a boat ramp, a fishing pier, a playground and a view of the big river traffic.
buzz: The river is the draw, with tugs and barges sliding past. Free and easy.

name: Voorhees College Historic District
unique: A historically Black college campus with Victorian brick buildings, a registered historic district and the story of Elizabeth Evelyn Wright, who founded it.
buzz: The campus is quiet and the history is remarkable. Check in at the administration building.

name: Bamberg Railroad Depot
unique: A restored small town depot on the old Southern Railway line, with a platform and a telegraph office feel, in a town built by the railroad and cotton.
buzz: A quick photo stop with the museum next door. The tracks are still active.

name: Salkehatchie River Swamp
unique: A dark, cypress lined swamp river with sandbars, oxbows and no development, one of the wildest blackwater corridors in the state.
buzz: The water is high in spring and the fishing is good. Bring a map, because the channels braid.

name: Barnwell County Courthouse
unique: A Victorian courthouse with a clock tower on a square of old storefronts, in the town that once called itself the best little town in the world.
buzz: A five minute look on the way to Healing Springs. The square is quiet.

name: Calhoun County Courthouse
unique: A neoclassical courthouse with columns and a dome on a small town square, in the county where the Congaree bluffs meet the coastal plain.
buzz: A quick stop with the museum nearby. The square has the bones of a cotton town.

name: St. Matthews Downtown
unique: A short main street of brick storefronts and a railroad crossing, with the county museum and the courthouse within a block.
buzz: It is a ten minute walk, and that is the whole town. Fine as a leg stretch.
